applies_why: The judge text makes an ambiguity in Matthew 1:16 the ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse. It is not, if the judge names another verse or phrase that settles it.
room: It is not, if the judge names another verse or phrase that settles it — requiring a named settling verse or phrase beyond the ambiguous verse versus accepting generic references to round arguments; I weighed those readings.
why: The judge declares Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because hēs with egennēthē admits both readings, without naming a different verse or phrase that settles it.
